Phase 2 › Block A › Step 01/11

Concepts — EC2 Foundations

Why this step matters: Run private, supportable EC2 instances and reason from instance health to application health.

01. EC2 mental model

A virtual server backed by an AMI, ENI, EBS root volume, IAM role and subnet placement. Instance state is not application health.

02. Instance families & sizing

Choose compute-, memory-, storage- or general-purpose families from workload evidence, not habit. Benchmark and right-size.

03. AMI & boot sequence

AMI defines launchable machine state; boot then runs OS/systemd/cloud-init and finally the application.

04. User Data

Bootstrap at first launch. Keep it small, idempotent and observable; long bootstrap belongs in a baked image or configuration system.

05. ENI & addressing

Private IP belongs to the ENI. Security groups attach to ENIs/resources; subnet and route table determine path.

06. IAM instance profile

EC2 assumes a role and receives short-lived credentials. Never place long-lived AWS keys on the instance.

07. SSM administration

Session Manager, Run Command and Patch Manager avoid direct inbound SSH and centralise audit/control.

08. IMDSv2

Session-oriented metadata access reduces SSRF credential-exposure risk. Require IMDSv2 unless a documented legacy dependency exists.

COMMON PRODUCTION MISTAKES

  • × Giving EC2 public IPs only for administration
  • × Using static AWS keys instead of IAM roles
  • × Leaving IMDSv1 enabled without a requirement
  • × Treating successful EC2 launch as proof the app is healthy
  • × Hard-coding instance IDs or IPs into deployment logic

Terraform — EC2 Foundations

Production Terraform is resources + relationships + state/rollout—not isolated snippets.

Production resources

aws_instanceaws_iam_roleaws_iam_instance_profileaws_iam_role_policy_attachmentaws_security_groupdata.aws_ami

Resource relationships

data.aws_ami → aws_instance ← aws_iam_instance_profile ← aws_iam_role
aws_instance → private subnet + application SG
SSM access → instance role + agent + network path/endpoints

Representative Terraform

data "aws_ami" "base" {
  most_recent = true
  owners      = ["amazon"]
  filter {
    name   = "name"
    values = ["al2023-ami-*-x86_64"]
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "ec2" {
  name = "phase2-ec2-role"
  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect = "Allow"
      Principal = { Service = "ec2.amazonaws.com" }
      Action = "sts:AssumeRole"
    }]
  })
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "ssm" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.ec2.name
  policy_arn = "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore"
}

resource "aws_iam_instance_profile" "ec2" {
  name = "phase2-ec2-profile"
  role = aws_iam_role.ec2.name
}

resource "aws_instance" "app" {
  ami                    = data.aws_ami.base.id
  instance_type          = "t3.small"
  subnet_id              = var.private_subnet_id
  vpc_security_group_ids = [var.app_sg_id]
  iam_instance_profile   = aws_iam_instance_profile.ec2.name

  metadata_options {
    http_endpoint = "enabled"
    http_tokens   = "required"
  }

  root_block_device {
    encrypted   = true
    volume_type = "gp3"
    volume_size = 20
  }
}
Rollout rule: fmt → validate → plan → PR/policy review → controlled apply → architecture verification → traffic/data verification.

Troubleshoot — EC2 Foundations

Use evidence before changing configuration.

IMPACT → SCOPE → RECENT CHANGE → EXPECTED PATH → EVIDENCE → HYPOTHESES → MITIGATE → ROOT CAUSE → PREVENT → VERIFY
1. Split host health from app health: status checks → OS → listener → SG/path → dependency
2. Use EC2 console output/system log, journalctl, systemctl, ss, curl localhost, CloudWatch and SSM
3. Compare a healthy instance with the failing instance before changing multiple variables

Q01L1EC2 basicsEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

What is an EC2 instance?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 30–60 sec

An EC2 instance is a virtual server running on AWS compute infrastructure. I choose an AMI and instance type, place it in a subnet, attach security groups and storage, and normally give it an IAM role rather than static credentials. In production I treat the instance as replaceable compute: configuration comes from images or bootstrap, health is monitored, and state is kept outside the host where possible.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

data.aws_amiaws_launch_templateaws_security_groupaws_iam_roleaws_iam_instance_profileaws_cloudwatch_log_group

Resource relationships

AMI and launch configuration are immutable inputs to the Launch Template. The template references the application Security Group and IAM instance profile; instances are launched without public IPv4. Bootstrap is version-controlled and its logs are shipped to CloudWatch so a failed user-data run is observable.

Production pattern

Use a Launch Template even when the first lab launches only one instance. Keep AMI selection, instance sizing and bootstrap in code; use IMDSv2, encrypted gp3 root volumes, instance roles and SSM instead of SSH/static credentials.

Representative Terraform

data "aws_ami" "app" {
  most_recent = true
  owners      = ["amazon"]

  filter {
    name   = "name"
    values = ["al2023-ami-*-x86_64"]
  }
}

resource "aws_launch_template" "app" {
  name_prefix   = "app-"
  image_id      = data.aws_ami.app.id
  instance_type = var.instance_type

  network_interfaces {
    associate_public_ip_address = false
    security_groups             = [aws_security_group.app.id]
  }

  iam_instance_profile { name = aws_iam_instance_profile.app.name }
  metadata_options {
    http_endpoint = "enabled"
    http_tokens   = "required"
  }

  block_device_mappings {
    device_name = "/dev/xvda"
    ebs { encrypted = true, volume_type = "gp3", volume_size = 30 }
  }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Plan must show an in-place/new Launch Template version, not an unexpected instance recreation unless intended. After rollout verify private addressing, IMDSv2, IAM role, SSM registration, EBS encryption and application/bootstrap logs.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Verify instance state + system/instance status checks, ENI/subnet/SG, IAM role attachment, IMDSv2, EBS health, SSM reachability and application listener. Do not equate 'running' with application healthy.
Source / Provenance EPAM

Candidate-reported interview collection

Reported AWS/DevOps rounds include EC2, AMI vs snapshot, user_data, instance profiles/families, Auto Scaling, Image Builder, CloudWatch, S3/Flow Logs and Terraform.

Q02L1Instance familiesRocketRouteSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Which EC2 instance families have you used?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 30–60 sec

I choose an EC2 family from the workload profile, not from habit. General-purpose workloads often fit M, compute-heavy workloads C, memory-heavy workloads R/X, burstable non-steady workloads T, and GPU/ML workloads use accelerated families. I then validate CPU, memory, network and EBS behaviour with metrics and right-size rather than assuming the first choice is correct.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

data.aws_amiaws_launch_templateaws_security_groupaws_iam_roleaws_iam_instance_profileaws_cloudwatch_log_group

Resource relationships

AMI and launch configuration are immutable inputs to the Launch Template. The template references the application Security Group and IAM instance profile; instances are launched without public IPv4. Bootstrap is version-controlled and its logs are shipped to CloudWatch so a failed user-data run is observable.

Production pattern

Use a Launch Template even when the first lab launches only one instance. Keep AMI selection, instance sizing and bootstrap in code; use IMDSv2, encrypted gp3 root volumes, instance roles and SSM instead of SSH/static credentials.

Representative Terraform

variable "instance_type" { type = string }

resource "aws_launch_template" "app" {
  image_id      = data.aws_ami.app.id
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  metadata_options { http_tokens = "required" }
}

# Keep sizing as an environment input; use CloudWatch/Compute Optimizer
# evidence to change the value through review rather than console resizing.

Plan · rollout · verification

Plan must show an in-place/new Launch Template version, not an unexpected instance recreation unless intended. After rollout verify private addressing, IMDSv2, IAM role, SSM registration, EBS encryption and application/bootstrap logs.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Check CPUUtilization, memory from CloudWatch Agent, network, EBS latency/queue, steal/load at OS level, and price/performance. Compare p95/p99 behaviour before and after a resize.

Q03L1User DataEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

What is EC2 user_data used for?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 30–60 sec

EC2 user_data is bootstrap input executed at instance launch, commonly through cloud-init. I use it for lightweight, deterministic startup such as installing the SSM/CloudWatch agent, fetching configuration, or starting a service. For production I keep it short and idempotent; large slow bootstrap belongs in a baked AMI because long user data increases rollout time and ASG failure risk.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

data.aws_amiaws_launch_templateaws_security_groupaws_iam_roleaws_iam_instance_profileaws_cloudwatch_log_group

Resource relationships

AMI and launch configuration are immutable inputs to the Launch Template. The template references the application Security Group and IAM instance profile; instances are launched without public IPv4. Bootstrap is version-controlled and its logs are shipped to CloudWatch so a failed user-data run is observable.

Production pattern

Use a Launch Template even when the first lab launches only one instance. Keep AMI selection, instance sizing and bootstrap in code; use IMDSv2, encrypted gp3 root volumes, instance roles and SSM instead of SSH/static credentials.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_launch_template" "app" {
  image_id      = data.aws_ami.app.id
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  user_data = base64encode(templatefile("${path.module}/bootstrap.sh.tftpl", {
    region = var.region
  }))
  metadata_options { http_tokens = "required" }
}

resource "aws_cloudwatch_log_group" "bootstrap" {
  name              = "/platform/bootstrap"
  retention_in_days = 30
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Plan must show an in-place/new Launch Template version, not an unexpected instance recreation unless intended. After rollout verify private addressing, IMDSv2, IAM role, SSM registration, EBS encryption and application/bootstrap logs.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Inspect /var/log/cloud-init.log and cloud-init-output.log, systemd status, package/network dependencies and application health. Re-run only if the script is idempotent; otherwise replace the instance.
Source / Provenance EPAM

Q04L2Instance identityEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

How do EC2 instance profiles work?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

An instance profile is the container that lets EC2 assume an IAM role. The application retrieves temporary credentials through the instance metadata service and the AWS SDK refreshes them automatically. In production I attach one least-privilege role per workload boundary, enforce IMDSv2, avoid static access keys, and scope permissions to exact APIs and resources.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_iam_roleaws_iam_role_policyaws_iam_instance_profileaws_launch_template

Resource relationships

The EC2 Launch Template references an instance profile. The profile contains an IAM role whose trust policy permits ec2.amazonaws.com. Applications obtain short-lived credentials from IMDSv2; permissions come from the role policy, not embedded access keys.

Production pattern

Create one least-privilege workload role per responsibility boundary. Require IMDSv2, avoid wildcard actions/resources, and separate deployer permissions from runtime permissions.

Representative Terraform

data "aws_iam_policy_document" "ec2_trust" {
  statement {
    actions = ["sts:AssumeRole"]
    principals { type = "Service", identifiers = ["ec2.amazonaws.com"] }
  }
}
resource "aws_iam_role" "app" {
  name               = "app-runtime"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.ec2_trust.json
}
resource "aws_iam_instance_profile" "app" {
  name = "app-runtime"
  role = aws_iam_role.app.name
}
resource "aws_launch_template" "app" {
  iam_instance_profile { name = aws_iam_instance_profile.app.name }
  metadata_options { http_tokens = "required" }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Confirm the instance profile is attached, IMDSv2 token requests succeed, STS identity is the expected role and denied API calls match least-privilege policy intent. CloudTrail should show the assumed-role principal.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Verify role trust, attached policies, instance-profile association, IMDSv2 token access and CloudTrail AccessDenied events. Test with sts get-caller-identity from the instance.
Source / Provenance EPAM

Q05L2Private computeEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

How can a private EC2 receive inbound traffic without NAT?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

A NAT Gateway is outbound-only, so I would not use it for inbound traffic. I would place an internet-facing ALB in public subnets and register the private EC2 instances as targets. The EC2 security group accepts only the application port from the ALB security group; administration stays private through SSM.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_lbaws_lb_target_groupaws_lb_listeneraws_launch_templateaws_autoscaling_groupaws_security_groupaws_iam_instance_profile

Resource relationships

The internet-facing ALB owns the public entry path; application instances remain in private subnets. ALB-SG permits client HTTPS, APP-SG permits only the target port from ALB-SG. The ASG spans private subnets in multiple AZs and registers instances in the target group; health checks determine serving/replacement state.

Production pattern

Separate edge, compute and administration paths. Do not use NAT for inbound traffic. Manage hosts through SSM, keep the fleet replaceable, externalize state, and use controlled ASG refresh or blue/green target groups for migration/deployment.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_lb" "app" {
  name               = "app-alb"
  internal           = false
  load_balancer_type = "application"
  subnets            = var.public_subnet_ids
  security_groups    = [aws_security_group.alb.id]
}
resource "aws_launch_template" "app" {
  image_id      = var.ami_id
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  network_interfaces {
    associate_public_ip_address = false
    security_groups             = [aws_security_group.app.id]
  }
  metadata_options { http_tokens = "required" }
}
resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "app" {
  min_size            = 2
  desired_capacity    = 2
  max_size            = 8
  vpc_zone_identifier = var.private_subnet_ids
  target_group_arns   = [aws_lb_target_group.app.arn]
  launch_template { id = aws_launch_template.app.id, version = "$Latest" }
  health_check_type         = "ELB"
  health_check_grace_period = 300
}
resource "aws_lb_listener" "https" {
  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.app.arn
  port              = 443
  protocol          = "HTTPS"
  ssl_policy        = "ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06"
  certificate_arn   = var.certificate_arn
  default_action { type = "forward", target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.app.arn }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Review subnet placement, SG references, listener certificate, target-group health and ASG replacement settings in plan. After apply test HTTPS through the ALB, confirm no instance public IPs, validate SSM access, target health, AZ distribution and rollback path.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Check DNS→ALB, listener/rule, target health, ALB SG, EC2 SG reference, application listener/health endpoint and return path. Confirm EC2 has no public IPv4.
Source / Provenance EPAM

Q06L2MonitoringCMTSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Which metrics monitor EC2 CPU and memory?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

EC2 publishes CPU, network, status-check and related infrastructure metrics natively, but memory utilisation is not a default EC2 metric. For memory, filesystem and process metrics I install and configure the CloudWatch Agent. I alert on service-level symptoms as well as host metrics so a healthy CPU graph does not hide an unavailable application.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_cloudwatch_log_groupaws_cloudwatch_metric_alarmaws_iam_roleaws_iam_instance_profileaws_ssm_associationaws_sns_topic

Resource relationships

Native EC2 metrics provide CPU, network and status checks. The CloudWatch Agent on the instance publishes memory/disk and application logs. Alarms route actionable signals to the operations topic; SSM provides controlled host access and agent configuration without opening SSH.

Production pattern

Monitor user-visible availability and dependency health, not CPU alone. Standardize CloudWatch Agent configuration through SSM, define alarms as code and attach runbooks/dashboard links to alerts.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_cloudwatch_log_group" "app" {
  name              = "/platform/app"
  retention_in_days = 30
}
resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "cpu_high" {
  alarm_name          = "app-cpu-high"
  namespace           = "AWS/EC2"
  metric_name         = "CPUUtilization"
  statistic           = "Average"
  period              = 300
  evaluation_periods  = 3
  threshold           = 80
  comparison_operator = "GreaterThanThreshold"
  dimensions          = { AutoScalingGroupName = var.asg_name }
  alarm_actions       = [aws_sns_topic.ops.arn]
}
resource "aws_ssm_association" "cloudwatch_agent" {
  name = "AmazonCloudWatch-ManageAgent"
  targets { key = "tag:Role", values = ["app"] }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Validate metric dimensions and periods before apply. Generate a controlled test signal, confirm alarm state transition and notification delivery, verify memory/disk custom metrics and confirm SSM can reach the same hosts during an incident.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Verify the metric namespace and dimensions, agent status/config, IAM permissions, alarm state and missing-data treatment. Correlate host metrics with ALB target health and application latency/errors.
Source / Provenance CMT

Q07L2Linux incidentCMTSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

A Linux server goes down: which commands do you run?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

I start with impact and whether the host itself is reachable. Then I check uptime/load, CPU and memory pressure, disk and inode exhaustion, network sockets/routes/DNS, failed systemd units and recent logs. I correlate that with EC2 status checks and CloudWatch, mitigate customer impact first—usually replace or fail over a disposable host—then complete RCA instead of debugging indefinitely on one server.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_cloudwatch_log_groupaws_cloudwatch_metric_alarmaws_iam_roleaws_iam_instance_profileaws_ssm_associationaws_sns_topic

Resource relationships

Native EC2 metrics provide CPU, network and status checks. The CloudWatch Agent on the instance publishes memory/disk and application logs. Alarms route actionable signals to the operations topic; SSM provides controlled host access and agent configuration without opening SSH.

Production pattern

Monitor user-visible availability and dependency health, not CPU alone. Standardize CloudWatch Agent configuration through SSM, define alarms as code and attach runbooks/dashboard links to alerts.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_cloudwatch_log_group" "app" {
  name              = "/platform/app"
  retention_in_days = 30
}
resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "cpu_high" {
  alarm_name          = "app-cpu-high"
  namespace           = "AWS/EC2"
  metric_name         = "CPUUtilization"
  statistic           = "Average"
  period              = 300
  evaluation_periods  = 3
  threshold           = 80
  comparison_operator = "GreaterThanThreshold"
  dimensions          = { AutoScalingGroupName = var.asg_name }
  alarm_actions       = [aws_sns_topic.ops.arn]
}
resource "aws_ssm_association" "cloudwatch_agent" {
  name = "AmazonCloudWatch-ManageAgent"
  targets { key = "tag:Role", values = ["app"] }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Validate metric dimensions and periods before apply. Generate a controlled test signal, confirm alarm state transition and notification delivery, verify memory/disk custom metrics and confirm SSM can reach the same hosts during an incident.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Commands: uptime/top or ps, free, df -h/df -i, ss -lntp, ip addr/route, resolvectl/dig, systemctl --failed/status, journalctl, dmesg. Compare with EC2 status checks and CloudWatch evidence.
Source / Provenance CMT

Q08L2Application incidentDeloitteSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

EC2 is healthy but the web app is unreachable. Why?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

If EC2 is healthy but the web application is unreachable, I separate infrastructure health from application health. I trace DNS and load-balancer health, then security groups/routes, then confirm the process is running and listening on the expected IP/port, inspect application logs and dependencies. I compare a healthy instance with the failing one and use evidence before changing configuration.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_lbaws_lb_target_groupaws_lb_listeneraws_launch_templateaws_autoscaling_groupaws_security_groupaws_iam_instance_profile

Resource relationships

The internet-facing ALB owns the public entry path; application instances remain in private subnets. ALB-SG permits client HTTPS, APP-SG permits only the target port from ALB-SG. The ASG spans private subnets in multiple AZs and registers instances in the target group; health checks determine serving/replacement state.

Production pattern

Separate edge, compute and administration paths. Do not use NAT for inbound traffic. Manage hosts through SSM, keep the fleet replaceable, externalize state, and use controlled ASG refresh or blue/green target groups for migration/deployment.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_lb" "app" {
  name               = "app-alb"
  internal           = false
  load_balancer_type = "application"
  subnets            = var.public_subnet_ids
  security_groups    = [aws_security_group.alb.id]
}
resource "aws_launch_template" "app" {
  image_id      = var.ami_id
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  network_interfaces {
    associate_public_ip_address = false
    security_groups             = [aws_security_group.app.id]
  }
  metadata_options { http_tokens = "required" }
}
resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "app" {
  min_size            = 2
  desired_capacity    = 2
  max_size            = 8
  vpc_zone_identifier = var.private_subnet_ids
  target_group_arns   = [aws_lb_target_group.app.arn]
  launch_template { id = aws_launch_template.app.id, version = "$Latest" }
  health_check_type         = "ELB"
  health_check_grace_period = 300
}
resource "aws_lb_listener" "https" {
  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.app.arn
  port              = 443
  protocol          = "HTTPS"
  ssl_policy        = "ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06"
  certificate_arn   = var.certificate_arn
  default_action { type = "forward", target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.app.arn }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Review subnet placement, SG references, listener certificate, target-group health and ASG replacement settings in plan. After apply test HTTPS through the ALB, confirm no instance public IPs, validate SSM access, target health, AZ distribution and rollback path.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Check ALB 4xx/5xx/target-response metrics, target reason codes, ss -lntp, curl localhost, SG/NACL/route path, systemd/app logs, DNS and downstream DB/API connectivity.
Source / Provenance Deloitte

Q09L2EC2 architectureDeloitteSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

From an empty AWS account, expose an EC2 service safely.

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

From an empty account I would first create the network and identity baseline, then put an internet-facing ALB in public subnets and the application instances in private subnets across at least two AZs. Only the ALB is internet-reachable; EC2 accepts traffic only from the ALB SG and is managed with SSM. I add TLS, health checks, logging, least-privilege IAM and IaC before exposing production traffic.

Q10L3MigrationJPMorganChaseSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Migrate public-subnet EC2 to private subnets without downtime; include rollback.

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

I would build the private fleet in parallel, not move production instances in place. I create private subnets/routes, launch the same application through a versioned launch template, validate it behind the existing/new ALB, then shift traffic gradually. Rollback is traffic reversal to the old public fleet until the private fleet is proven, after which public IPs and obsolete rules are removed.

Q11L3HA architectureCMTSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Design a highly available, fault-tolerant AWS system.

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

For high availability I remove single-instance and single-AZ dependencies: multi-AZ load balancing, an ASG across multiple private subnets, health-based replacement and externalised state. I design each dependency for its required availability, monitor user-facing SLIs, and test instance/AZ failure. Fault tolerance means the service continues through expected failures, not merely that resources exist in two AZs.

Q12L3DeploymentJPMorganChaseSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

How do you deploy an application to AWS?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

I deploy by separating application build from infrastructure delivery. CI produces an immutable, versioned artefact or image; Terraform changes infrastructure through reviewed plans; deployment uses a controlled strategy such as rolling, blue-green or canary with health gates. Credentials are short-lived, production changes are auditable, and rollback points to the previous known-good artefact/configuration.

Q13L3Deployment strategyJPMorganChaseSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

How have you implemented blue-green deployment?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

For blue-green I maintain two production-capable environments behind separate target groups. I deploy and validate green without customer traffic, then shift traffic using the load balancer or DNS in a controlled step. Blue remains untouched during the observation window, so rollback is a traffic switch rather than rebuilding infrastructure.

Concepts — EBS + AMI + Storage Performance

Why this step matters: Operate the EC2 disk layer safely: performance, encryption, resize, snapshot, restore and image distribution.

01. EBS mental model

Persistent block storage attached to EC2. A normal EBS volume is scoped to one Availability Zone.

02. gp3 vs io2

gp3 decouples size, IOPS and throughput for general workloads; io2 targets demanding, latency-sensitive and durability-focused workloads.

03. IOPS vs throughput vs latency

IOPS is operation rate, throughput is bytes/time, latency is response time. Diagnose the workload pattern before changing volume type.

04. Filesystem layer

Increasing the EBS device does not necessarily expand the partition/filesystem. Verify lsblk, growpart and filesystem-specific expansion.

05. Snapshots

Incremental point-in-time EBS backups stored by AWS. Restore creates a new volume; test recovery rather than assuming a snapshot equals DR.

06. Encryption & KMS

Encryption covers EBS data at rest, snapshots and data moving between instance and volume. Key policy/IAM can still break attachment/restore.

07. AMI vs snapshot

A snapshot is volume data; an AMI is a launchable image definition that references snapshots plus boot metadata.

08. Image lifecycle

Build → scan → test → approve → distribute → launch-template version → controlled fleet rollout → retire old image.

COMMON PRODUCTION MISTAKES

  • × Assuming EBS is regional rather than AZ-scoped
  • × Increasing volume size but forgetting partition/filesystem growth
  • × Choosing volume type without IOPS/throughput evidence
  • × Keeping legacy unencrypted data after enabling default encryption
  • × Having snapshots but never testing restore

Q14L1AMI / SnapshotEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

AMI versus EBS snapshot: what is the difference?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 30–60 sec

An EBS snapshot is a point-in-time backup of an individual EBS volume. An AMI is a launchable EC2 image definition that includes boot metadata and references one or more snapshots. I use snapshots primarily for volume backup/restore and AMIs for repeatable instance creation or golden-image workflows.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_ebs_volumeaws_volume_attachmentaws_ebs_snapshotaws_kms_keyaws_instance

Resource relationships

EBS volumes and the EC2 instance must be in the same Availability Zone. The attachment references both resources explicitly. Snapshots are the portable recovery primitive; an AMI adds launch metadata and one or more snapshot-backed block-device mappings.

Production pattern

Use encrypted gp3 by default, size IOPS/throughput from workload evidence, snapshot before risky storage changes, and restore into the target AZ rather than attempting cross-AZ attachment.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_kms_key" "ebs" {
  description         = "EBS encryption key"
  enable_key_rotation = true
}
resource "aws_ebs_volume" "data" {
  availability_zone = aws_instance.app.availability_zone
  size              = 100
  type              = "gp3"
  encrypted         = true
  kms_key_id        = aws_kms_key.ebs.arn
  tags              = { Name = "app-data" }
}
resource "aws_volume_attachment" "data" {
  device_name = "/dev/sdf"
  volume_id   = aws_ebs_volume.data.id
  instance_id = aws_instance.app.id
}
resource "aws_ebs_snapshot" "data" {
  volume_id   = aws_ebs_volume.data.id
  description = "pre-change snapshot"
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Plan must not move an EBS volume across AZs. Verify encryption/KMS access, attachment state, filesystem mount, free space and I/O metrics. For restore, create a fresh volume from snapshot, mount it and validate application data before cutover.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
For AMI, launch a test instance and verify boot/application. For snapshots, perform a restore, attach/mount the volume and validate data. A successful snapshot API call is not a tested recovery.
Source / Provenance EPAM

Reported AWS/DevOps rounds include EC2, AMI vs snapshot, user_data, instance profiles/families, Auto Scaling, Image Builder, CloudWatch, S3/Flow Logs and Terraform.

Q15L1Image lifecycleEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

What is EC2 Image Builder?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 30–60 sec

EC2 Image Builder automates creation, testing and distribution of hardened machine images. In production I use a controlled base image, versioned build components, patching and security tests, then publish the resulting AMI to approved accounts/regions. Workloads consume an explicit approved image version rather than manually maintained servers.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_imagebuilder_image_pipelineaws_imagebuilder_image_recipeaws_imagebuilder_infrastructure_configurationaws_imagebuilder_distribution_configurationaws_launch_template

Resource relationships

The image recipe pins a parent image and hardening/install components. The pipeline builds/tests through the infrastructure configuration, publishes a versioned AMI and distributes it to required accounts/regions. Launch Templates consume the approved AMI version.

Production pattern

Treat AMIs as immutable release artifacts. Build on a schedule or source change, run security/functional tests, tag with provenance and update fleets only after an approved image passes.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_imagebuilder_image_recipe" "app" {
  name         = "app"
  version      = "1.0.0"
  parent_image = var.base_ami_arn
  component { component_arn = var.hardening_component_arn }
}
resource "aws_imagebuilder_image_pipeline" "app" {
  name                             = "app"
  image_recipe_arn                 = aws_imagebuilder_image_recipe.app.arn
  infrastructure_configuration_arn = aws_imagebuilder_infrastructure_configuration.app.arn
  distribution_configuration_arn   = aws_imagebuilder_distribution_configuration.app.arn
}
# Approved output AMI becomes the image_id input to the Launch Template.

Plan · rollout · verification

Validate component versions and distribution targets in plan. After a build confirm test success, AMI tags/provenance, encryption and sharing; launch a canary instance before updating the ASG Launch Template.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Verify build/test stages, component logs, AMI encryption/share permissions, launch test and vulnerability baseline. Roll out via a new launch-template version and controlled instance refresh.
Source / Provenance EPAM

Q16L1Storage choiceMotivity LabsSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Explain EBS versus EFS.

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 30–60 sec

EBS is block storage attached to compute in the same AZ and is suitable for boot volumes, databases and low-latency single-host filesystems. EFS is a managed shared NFS filesystem accessible from multiple instances across AZs through mount targets. I choose based on access semantics first—block versus shared file—then performance, availability and cost.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_efs_file_systemaws_efs_mount_targetaws_security_groupaws_ebs_volumeaws_s3_bucketaws_backup_selection

Resource relationships

EBS is attached to one AZ-local EC2 workload as block storage. EFS exposes a regional filesystem through mount targets in each workload AZ and Security Groups permit NFS/2049 only from the application SG. S3 is used for object data rather than mounted block/file semantics.

Production pattern

Choose storage from access semantics first: EBS for low-latency block, EFS for shared POSIX/NFS, S3 for durable object storage. Encrypt all three and protect state with backup/versioning/lifecycle appropriate to the data class.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_efs_file_system" "shared" {
  encrypted = true
}
resource "aws_efs_mount_target" "az" {
  for_each        = var.private_subnets
  file_system_id  = aws_efs_file_system.shared.id
  subnet_id       = each.value
  security_groups = [aws_security_group.efs.id]
}
resource "aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule" "nfs" {
  security_group_id            = aws_security_group.efs.id
  referenced_security_group_id = aws_security_group.app.id
  from_port = 2049
  to_port   = 2049
  ip_protocol = "tcp"
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Verify mount targets exist in every active AZ, SG permits TCP/2049 only from expected clients, DNS resolves the EFS endpoint and failover works after terminating one EC2 host. For EBS verify AZ/IOPS; for S3 verify object-policy/KMS behaviour.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
EBS: verify AZ, device/filesystem, IOPS/throughput and attachment. EFS: DNS, mount target in reachable AZ/VPC, SG 2049, NFS client, mount options and throughput metrics.
Source / Provenance Motivity Labs

Candidate-reported Glassdoor interview

Reported Senior DevOps interview includes high CPU/memory triage, Terraform drift/environments/modules, EBS vs EFS and EBS AZ attachment constraints.

Q20L2Fleet inventoryCocusSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

List each server and its EBS size with Boto3; automate it.

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

I would enumerate the required accounts and regions using an assumed read-only role, call describe_instances and describe_volumes with pagination, join volumes to instance attachments, and output a structured inventory. For production automation I include retries, rate-limit handling, clear account/region context, and export to CSV/S3 or an inventory store rather than printing ad hoc output.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_iam_roleaws_iam_role_policyaws_lambda_functionaws_s3_bucketaws_glue_catalog_tableaws_athena_workgroup

Resource relationships

A central inventory runner assumes a read-only role in each Organization account, calls EC2 DescribeInstances/DescribeVolumes, normalizes the data and writes dated output to a central encrypted S3 bucket. Athena/Glue provide queryable inventory without broad console access.

Production pattern

Provision the cross-account roles and evidence store with Terraform; keep the Boto3 collector as application code. Scope sts:AssumeRole to the organization/accounts and EC2 read APIs only.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_iam_role" "inventory" {
  name               = "central-inventory-reader"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.inventory_trust.json
}
resource "aws_s3_bucket" "inventory" { bucket = var.inventory_bucket }
resource "aws_s3_bucket_versioning" "inventory" {
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.inventory.id
  versioning_configuration { status = "Enabled" }
}
resource "aws_lambda_function" "collector" {
  function_name = "ec2-ebs-inventory"
  role          = aws_iam_role.collector_exec.arn
  handler       = "handler.lambda_handler"
  runtime       = "python3.13"
  filename      = var.collector_zip
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Test against one non-production account first. Confirm assumed-role identity, pagination, region iteration and encryption. Compare a sample of collected instances/volumes with the EC2 API, then schedule centrally and alarm on stale/missing inventory.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Validate pagination, unattached volumes, multiple block devices, encrypted volumes, stopped instances, all regions and permission failures. Reconcile sample output against the EC2 console/API.
Source / Provenance Cocus

To share an AMI cross-account I grant launch permissions on the AMI and ensure the backing snapshots and KMS key policy allow the destination account when encrypted. In many production environments I then copy the AMI into the destination account/region so ownership, encryption and lifecycle are local. I automate distribution rather than sharing images manually.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_ami_launch_permissionaws_kms_grantaws_ami_copyaws_launch_template

Resource relationships

The source account grants AMI launch permission and, for encrypted snapshots, KMS access to the target. The target account copies the AMI so it owns the image/snapshots and can independently lifecycle/version it before Launch Template use.

Production pattern

Prefer target-account AMI copies over indefinite cross-account dependency. Distribute only approved images, retain provenance tags and automate retirement of old copies.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_ami_launch_permission" "target" {
  image_id   = var.source_ami_id
  account_id = var.target_account_id
}
# In the target-account provider:
resource "aws_ami_copy" "app" {
  provider          = aws.target
  name              = "app-${var.release}"
  source_ami_id     = var.source_ami_id
  source_ami_region = var.source_region
  encrypted         = true
  kms_key_id        = var.target_kms_key_arn
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Verify AMI and backing snapshot permissions plus KMS key policy before copy. In the target account confirm the copied AMI is Available and encrypted under the expected key, then launch a canary before updating production.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Test destination account can describe/copy/launch the image, decrypt snapshots and boot successfully. Verify revoked sharing does not break already-owned copies.
Source / Provenance Nielsen

Q22L2Backup operationsDeloitteSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

How do you back up AWS workloads?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

I design backup from business RPO/RTO, not simply 'enable snapshots'. I define what is protected, backup frequency and retention, encrypted vaults, cross-account/region copy where required, and—most importantly—scheduled restore testing. Backup success and disaster recovery are separate controls.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_backup_vaultaws_backup_planaws_backup_selectionaws_iam_roleaws_sns_topicaws_cloudwatch_event_rule

Resource relationships

The Backup plan defines schedule and lifecycle, selections bind tagged resources, and recovery points land in an encrypted vault. EventBridge/SNS and CloudTrail provide job/audit evidence; optional copy actions place recovery points in another vault/account/region.

Production pattern

Define policy by data class and RPO/RTO rather than ad-hoc snapshots. Separate backup administration from workload teams, protect vaults and perform scheduled restore tests.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_backup_vault" "prod" {
  name        = "prod-vault"
  kms_key_arn = var.backup_kms_key_arn
}
resource "aws_backup_plan" "prod" {
  name = "prod"
  rule {
    rule_name         = "daily"
    target_vault_name = aws_backup_vault.prod.name
    schedule          = "cron(0 2 * * ? *)"
    lifecycle { delete_after = 35 }
  }
}
resource "aws_backup_selection" "tagged" {
  name         = "prod-tagged"
  iam_role_arn = aws_iam_role.backup.arn
  plan_id      = aws_backup_plan.prod.id
  selection_tag { type = "STRINGEQUALS", key = "Backup", value = "daily" }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Plan should show policy changes, not workload replacement. Verify a recovery point is created, event/status evidence reaches operations, then perform a real restore into an isolated environment and measure achieved RTO/RPO.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Check backup job success, recovery-point age, retention/copy, IAM/KMS, and perform restore drills with data/application validation. Measure achieved RPO/RTO.
Source / Provenance Deloitte

Q23L3Fleet inventoryDeloitteSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Inventory running EC2 and EBS across 50–60 accounts.

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

At 50–60 accounts I avoid console-by-console inventory. I use Organizations account discovery plus a standard cross-account read role, iterate enabled regions, query EC2 and EBS APIs with pagination, and store normalized results centrally. I include owner/tags, age, state, attachment, size/type/encryption and cost-relevant fields so the inventory is operationally useful.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_iam_roleaws_iam_role_policyaws_lambda_functionaws_s3_bucketaws_glue_catalog_tableaws_athena_workgroup

Resource relationships

A central inventory runner assumes a read-only role in each Organization account, calls EC2 DescribeInstances/DescribeVolumes, normalizes the data and writes dated output to a central encrypted S3 bucket. Athena/Glue provide queryable inventory without broad console access.

Production pattern

Provision the cross-account roles and evidence store with Terraform; keep the Boto3 collector as application code. Scope sts:AssumeRole to the organization/accounts and EC2 read APIs only.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_iam_role" "inventory" {
  name               = "central-inventory-reader"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.inventory_trust.json
}
resource "aws_s3_bucket" "inventory" { bucket = var.inventory_bucket }
resource "aws_s3_bucket_versioning" "inventory" {
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.inventory.id
  versioning_configuration { status = "Enabled" }
}
resource "aws_lambda_function" "collector" {
  function_name = "ec2-ebs-inventory"
  role          = aws_iam_role.collector_exec.arn
  handler       = "handler.lambda_handler"
  runtime       = "python3.13"
  filename      = var.collector_zip
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Test against one non-production account first. Confirm assumed-role identity, pagination, region iteration and encryption. Compare a sample of collected instances/volumes with the EC2 API, then schedule centrally and alarm on stale/missing inventory.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Measure account/region coverage, API throttling/errors, stale data, missing tags and reconciliation against AWS Config/Resource Explorer samples. Alert when an account cannot be scanned.

Q26L3Storage integrationEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Where does AWS Storage Gateway fit?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

Storage Gateway is a hybrid-storage service used when on-premises applications need familiar file, volume or tape interfaces while data is backed by AWS storage. I would choose the gateway mode from the application protocol and migration/backup requirement; it is not a replacement for native S3/EFS access when the workload already runs in AWS.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_storagegateway_gatewayaws_storagegateway_cacheaws_storagegateway_nfs_file_shareaws_s3_bucketaws_iam_role

Resource relationships

The on-premises gateway appliance registers with AWS, uses local cache/upload-buffer disks and exposes NFS/SMB/iSCSI depending on gateway mode. The file share writes objects into a controlled S3 bucket using an IAM role.

Production pattern

Use Storage Gateway when applications need familiar on-prem file/block interfaces while durable data lands in AWS. Size cache/network for workload, encrypt transport/storage and monitor upload backlog.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_storagegateway_gateway" "file" {
  gateway_ip_address = var.gateway_ip
  gateway_name       = "onprem-file-gw"
  gateway_timezone   = "GMT"
  gateway_type       = "FILE_S3"
}
resource "aws_storagegateway_nfs_file_share" "share" {
  client_list  = var.allowed_clients
  gateway_arn  = aws_storagegateway_gateway.file.arn
  location_arn = "arn:aws:s3:::${aws_s3_bucket.archive.bucket}/"
  role_arn     = aws_iam_role.gateway.arn
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Verify gateway connectivity, local cache health, client allowlist, S3 object arrival and CloudWatch upload metrics. Test loss/recovery of WAN connectivity and confirm queued writes drain after recovery.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Validate appliance health, required outbound connectivity/DNS/time, cache capacity, share/volume permissions, upload backlog and end-to-end read/write from the on-prem client.

Phase 2 › Block C › Step 01/11

Concepts — Launch Templates + Auto Scaling

Why this step matters: Build disposable, multi-AZ EC2 fleets that scale and roll safely without making individual instances special.

01. Launch Template

Versioned launch specification: AMI, instance type, SGs, IAM profile, metadata, storage and user data.

02. ASG capacity

min is safety floor, desired is current target, max is guardrail. Select from availability and scaling requirements.

03. Multi-AZ placement

Distribute across private subnets/AZs and let the ASG replace failed capacity.

04. Health checks

EC2 health proves infrastructure; ELB health can reflect the application. Grace/warm-up must cover real startup time.

05. Target tracking

Scale around a measurable signal tied to load. Scheduled actions are useful for predictable demand.

06. Instance Refresh

Controlled replacement of old launch-template versions with healthy new instances and rollback/abort criteria.

07. Golden images

Bake slow/critical dependencies into tested AMIs to reduce boot time and drift.

08. Purchasing strategy

Keep a stable baseline on resilient capacity; use Spot for interruptible/flexible capacity with diversification and interruption handling.

COMMON PRODUCTION MISTAKES

  • × Changing launch-template AMI and assuming existing instances update
  • × Using EC2 health only when application health matters
  • × Bootstrapping for minutes when a baked image is safer
  • × Deploying all capacity in one AZ
  • × Keeping state on disposable ASG instances

Terraform — Launch Templates + Auto Scaling

Production Terraform is resources + relationships + state/rollout—not isolated snippets.

Production resources

aws_launch_templateaws_autoscaling_groupaws_autoscaling_policyaws_autoscaling_scheduleaws_autoscaling_attachmentaws_lb_target_groupaws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm

Resource relationships

AMI → Launch Template version → ASG across private subnets
ASG → target group → ALB health
CloudWatch metric → scaling policy → ASG desired capacity
Instance Refresh → controlled old→new fleet replacement

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_launch_template" "app" {
  name_prefix   = "phase2-app-"
  image_id      = var.ami_id
  instance_type = "t3.small"

  iam_instance_profile { name = var.instance_profile_name }
  vpc_security_group_ids = [var.app_sg_id]

  metadata_options {
    http_endpoint = "enabled"
    http_tokens   = "required"
  }
}

resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "app" {
  name                = "phase2-app"
  min_size            = 2
  desired_capacity    = 2
  max_size            = 8
  vpc_zone_identifier = var.private_subnet_ids
  target_group_arns   = [var.target_group_arn]
  health_check_type   = "ELB"
  health_check_grace_period = 180

  launch_template {
    id      = aws_launch_template.app.id
    version = "$Latest"
  }

  instance_refresh {
    strategy = "Rolling"
    preferences { min_healthy_percentage = 90 }
  }
}

resource "aws_autoscaling_policy" "cpu" {
  name                   = "phase2-target-tracking"
  autoscaling_group_name = aws_autoscaling_group.app.name
  policy_type            = "TargetTrackingScaling"
  target_tracking_configuration {
    predefined_metric_specification {
      predefined_metric_type = "ASGAverageCPUUtilization"
    }
    target_value = 55
  }
}
Rollout rule: fmt → validate → plan → PR/policy review → controlled apply → architecture verification → traffic/data verification.

Q27L1Auto ScalingEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Explain Auto Scaling Groups in AWS.

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 30–60 sec

An Auto Scaling Group maintains a desired EC2 fleet within min/max capacity, spreads it across configured subnets/AZs, replaces unhealthy instances and can scale from metrics or schedules. In production I pair it with a versioned launch template, application-aware health checks, sensible warm-up and controlled instance refresh so replacement is safe.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_launch_templateaws_autoscaling_groupaws_autoscaling_policyaws_lb_target_groupaws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm

Resource relationships

The Launch Template defines immutable instance configuration. The ASG owns fleet size and AZ distribution, registers capacity with the target group and uses ELB health for replacement. Scaling policies change desired capacity from measured load; warm-up/grace settings stop healthy-but-booting instances being recycled.

Production pattern

Keep min/desired/max, warm-up and health grace explicit per environment. Use target tracking for variable load and scheduled actions only when demand is genuinely predictable. Keep applications stateless so replacement is safe.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "app" {
  min_size            = var.min_size
  desired_capacity    = var.desired_capacity
  max_size            = var.max_size
  vpc_zone_identifier = var.private_subnet_ids
  target_group_arns   = [var.target_group_arn]
  health_check_type         = "ELB"
  health_check_grace_period = var.health_grace_seconds
  launch_template { id = aws_launch_template.app.id, version = "$Latest" }
}
resource "aws_autoscaling_policy" "cpu" {
  name                   = "cpu-target"
  autoscaling_group_name = aws_autoscaling_group.app.name
  policy_type            = "TargetTrackingScaling"
  estimated_instance_warmup = var.instance_warmup_seconds
  target_tracking_configuration {
    predefined_metric_specification { predefined_metric_type = "ASGAverageCPUUtilization" }
    target_value = 55
  }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Plan must show intended capacity/policy changes only. Generate controlled load, verify scale-out timing, target registration, warm-up and subsequent scale-in. Simulate one instance/AZ loss and confirm desired capacity and user traffic recover.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Terminate an instance and verify replacement; validate multi-AZ distribution, target health, scaling policy evaluation, warm-up/grace period and capacity during refresh.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 30–60 sec

Spot is discounted spare capacity that can be interrupted, so I use it for fault-tolerant, horizontally scalable capacity with diversification and graceful interruption handling. Reserved Instances or Savings Plans are commitment-based discounts for predictable usage; Savings Plans are generally more flexible. I keep enough non-interruptible baseline capacity for the service SLO.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

aws_launch_templateaws_autoscaling_groupaws_autoscaling_policy

Resource relationships

A mixed-instances ASG maintains an On-Demand baseline and uses diversified Spot capacity for burst. Allocation strategy spreads requests across eligible instance types/AZs and capacity rebalance replaces interrupted Spot instances proactively.

Production pattern

Do not put irreplaceable state on Spot. Use several compatible instance types, an On-Demand floor for SLO-critical baseline and Spot only for interruption-tolerant burst capacity.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "app" {
  min_size            = 4
  desired_capacity    = 6
  max_size            = 40
  capacity_rebalance  = true
  vpc_zone_identifier = var.private_subnet_ids

  mixed_instances_policy {
    instances_distribution {
      on_demand_base_capacity                  = 4
      on_demand_percentage_above_base_capacity = 20
      spot_allocation_strategy                 = "price-capacity-optimized"
    }
    launch_template {
      launch_template_specification { launch_template_id = aws_launch_template.app.id, version = "$Latest" }
      override { instance_type = "m7i.large" }
      override { instance_type = "m7a.large" }
      override { instance_type = "m6i.large" }
    }
  }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Verify the plan preserves diversification and On-Demand floor. During a load test inspect instance lifecycle/market mix and simulate Spot interruption handling. Compare cost and SLOs against an all-On-Demand baseline.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Test Spot interruption/rebalance behaviour, target draining, workload checkpointing and capacity fallback. Compare effective cost and SLO impact, not only hourly price.

Q29L1Auto ScalingJPMorganChaseSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Where are autoscaling parameters defined?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 30–60 sec

The launch template defines instance configuration, while the ASG defines min, desired and max capacity, subnets, health behaviour and fleet policy. Scaling policies or scheduled actions adjust desired capacity. I keep these responsibilities separate because changing an image is not the same as changing scaling thresholds.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_launch_templateaws_autoscaling_groupaws_autoscaling_policyaws_lb_target_groupaws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm

Resource relationships

The Launch Template defines immutable instance configuration. The ASG owns fleet size and AZ distribution, registers capacity with the target group and uses ELB health for replacement. Scaling policies change desired capacity from measured load; warm-up/grace settings stop healthy-but-booting instances being recycled.

Production pattern

Keep min/desired/max, warm-up and health grace explicit per environment. Use target tracking for variable load and scheduled actions only when demand is genuinely predictable. Keep applications stateless so replacement is safe.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "app" {
  min_size            = var.min_size
  desired_capacity    = var.desired_capacity
  max_size            = var.max_size
  vpc_zone_identifier = var.private_subnet_ids
  target_group_arns   = [var.target_group_arn]
  health_check_type         = "ELB"
  health_check_grace_period = var.health_grace_seconds
  launch_template { id = aws_launch_template.app.id, version = "$Latest" }
}
resource "aws_autoscaling_policy" "cpu" {
  name                   = "cpu-target"
  autoscaling_group_name = aws_autoscaling_group.app.name
  policy_type            = "TargetTrackingScaling"
  estimated_instance_warmup = var.instance_warmup_seconds
  target_tracking_configuration {
    predefined_metric_specification { predefined_metric_type = "ASGAverageCPUUtilization" }
    target_value = 55
  }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Plan must show intended capacity/policy changes only. Generate controlled load, verify scale-out timing, target registration, warm-up and subsequent scale-in. Simulate one instance/AZ loss and confirm desired capacity and user traffic recover.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Inspect ASG Activity History, desired/in-service/pending counts, policy status, CloudWatch metric and launch-template version. Verify who/what changed desired capacity through CloudTrail.

Q30L2Fleet rolloutEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Launch-template AMI changed: how do you deploy it to the fleet?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

Updating a launch template does not automatically replace already-running instances. I create a new launch-template version, point the ASG at it, and run a controlled instance refresh or deployment strategy with minimum healthy capacity and health checks. I monitor the rollout and retain the previous version for rollback.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_launch_templateaws_autoscaling_groupaws_lb_target_groupaws_lb_listener_ruleaws_autoscaling_group

Resource relationships

A new immutable AMI creates a new Launch Template version. Instance Refresh or a parallel green ASG introduces new capacity, ALB health checks gate serving, and rollback points the fleet/listener back to the previous known-good version.

Production pattern

Never mutate production instances in place for routine releases. Keep prior AMI/LT versions available, set minimum healthy percentage and checkpoints/canary validation before broad replacement.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "app" {
  # ... capacity and subnet settings ...
  launch_template { id = aws_launch_template.app.id, version = "$Latest" }

  instance_refresh {
    strategy = "Rolling"
    preferences {
      min_healthy_percentage = 90
      instance_warmup        = 300
    }
    triggers = ["launch_template"]
  }
}
resource "aws_launch_template" "app" {
  image_id = var.release_ami_id
  update_default_version = true
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Plan must expose the new AMI/LT version and refresh blast radius. Validate a canary target, ALB 5xx/latency/healthy-host metrics and application smoke tests before continuing. Roll back by restoring the prior Launch Template version or listener target.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Compare running instance image IDs/launch-template versions, ASG refresh status and target health. Abort/rollback on error or latency regression and restore previous template version.

Q35L2DeploymentRocketRouteSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Which deployment strategies have you used?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

I choose deployment strategy from availability and rollback requirements. Rolling uses less duplicate capacity but mixes versions during rollout. Blue-green gives a very fast traffic rollback but costs more and needs backward-compatible data changes. Canary reduces blast radius by exposing a small percentage first. I prefer immutable replacement over manual in-place changes for autoscaled fleets.
