Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

I would use list_objects_v2 with the Prefix parameter and a paginator rather than listing the whole bucket. If the exact naming contract is known, I avoid scanning and call head_object/get_object directly. The code uses an IAM role, handles no matches/multiple matches and streams large objects instead of loading everything into memory.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_s3_bucketaws_glue_catalog_databaseaws_glue_catalog_tableaws_athena_workgroupaws_iam_role

Resource relationships

Logs/objects land in partitioned S3 prefixes. Glue defines schema, Athena queries only required partitions/prefixes and stores results in a controlled bucket. The query role has read-only source access and write access only to the results prefix.

Production pattern

Use Boto3 ListObjectsV2 for targeted object discovery; use Athena for large log sets instead of downloading/grepping. Partition by date/account/region when volume is high and retain evidence immutably.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_athena_workgroup" "ops" {
  name = "ops"
  configuration {
    enforce_workgroup_configuration = true
    result_configuration { output_location = "s3://${aws_s3_bucket.query_results.bucket}/results/" }
  }
}
resource "aws_glue_catalog_database" "logs" { name = "platform_logs" }
# Define a table matching the actual log format and partition keys.
# Application/Boto3 code performs prefix discovery or parameterized queries.

Plan · rollout · verification

Validate one known object/IP against raw S3 before trusting automation. Check query role, partition pruning, scanned bytes/cost and time range. Preserve the query and result location for incident evidence.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Test zero/one/many matches, pagination >1000 objects, KMS-encrypted objects, AccessDenied and large-object streaming. Log bucket/key context without leaking sensitive content.

Q49L3Three-tier designGlobantSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Design storage choices for an AWS three-tier application.

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

I would not pick one storage service for the whole application. EC2 boot/local block needs EBS; shared POSIX content across instances may need EFS; static objects, artefacts, uploads and backups usually belong in S3. I keep transactional database state in the managed database tier. The decision is driven by access semantics, durability, latency, concurrency and cost.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_efs_file_systemaws_efs_mount_targetaws_security_groupaws_ebs_volumeaws_s3_bucketaws_backup_selection

Resource relationships

EBS is attached to one AZ-local EC2 workload as block storage. EFS exposes a regional filesystem through mount targets in each workload AZ and Security Groups permit NFS/2049 only from the application SG. S3 is used for object data rather than mounted block/file semantics.

Production pattern

Choose storage from access semantics first: EBS for low-latency block, EFS for shared POSIX/NFS, S3 for durable object storage. Encrypt all three and protect state with backup/versioning/lifecycle appropriate to the data class.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_efs_file_system" "shared" {
  encrypted = true
}
resource "aws_efs_mount_target" "az" {
  for_each        = var.private_subnets
  file_system_id  = aws_efs_file_system.shared.id
  subnet_id       = each.value
  security_groups = [aws_security_group.efs.id]
}
resource "aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule" "nfs" {
  security_group_id            = aws_security_group.efs.id
  referenced_security_group_id = aws_security_group.app.id
  from_port = 2049
  to_port   = 2049
  ip_protocol = "tcp"
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Verify mount targets exist in every active AZ, SG permits TCP/2049 only from expected clients, DNS resolves the EFS endpoint and failover works after terminating one EC2 host. For EBS verify AZ/IOPS; for S3 verify object-policy/KMS behaviour.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Test instance/AZ replacement, concurrent file access, object permissions, backup/restore, throughput and failure behaviour. Confirm state does not disappear when an EC2 instance is replaced.

resource "aws_s3_bucket" "data" { bucket = var.bucket_name }
resource "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block" "data" {
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.data.id
  block_public_acls       = true
  block_public_policy     = true
  ignore_public_acls      = true
  restrict_public_buckets = true
}
resource "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration" "data" {
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.data.id
  rule { apply_server_side_encryption_by_default {
    sse_algorithm     = "aws:kms"
    kms_master_key_id = aws_kms_key.s3.arn
  }}
}
# Bucket/IAM policies should scope exact actions, prefixes and principals.

Plan · rollout · verification

Use IAM policy simulation plus a real workload-role test. Confirm anonymous/public requests fail, approved prefix operations succeed, disallowed prefixes/KMS operations fail and CloudTrail/S3 audit evidence records the expected principal.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Test positive and negative cases with the real workload identity: allowed prefix works, adjacent prefix denied, delete denied if not needed, KMS works, anonymous/public access fails. Use CloudTrail data events for sensitive audit paths.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

I reuse Terraform through versioned modules while keeping each environment as a separate root configuration and state boundary. Inputs represent intentional differences—size, account, region, retention—not copy-pasted resource code. Production promotion uses reviewed module versions; I do not make dev and prod share one mutable state file.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

terraform_remote_state / backendmodule.networkmodule.computemodule.storageaws_iam_role

Resource relationships

Reusable modules expose stable inputs/outputs; environment root modules instantiate them. Each environment/team owns a separate state boundary and CI role, preventing a compute change from locking or replacing unrelated network/application resources.

Production pattern

Separate state by lifecycle/ownership/blast radius, not by arbitrary file size. Keep providers/backends in root modules, pin module/provider versions and use distinct accounts/roles for environment isolation.

Representative Terraform

# environments/prod/main.tf
module "compute" {
  source = "../../modules/compute"
  vpc_id             = var.vpc_id
  private_subnet_ids = var.private_subnet_ids

}

Run plan independently per environment, test module upgrade in lower environments, inspect state addresses before refactors and use moved/import blocks where needed. Confirm a prod plan cannot touch dev resources.

Q52L3Terraform driftMotivity LabsSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Someone changes AWS manually. What happens to Terraform?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

A manual AWS change creates drift between configuration/state expectations and reality. The next refresh/plan will usually detect it and propose changing AWS back to the declared configuration, or show another necessary action. I first determine whether the manual change was an approved emergency fix; then I either codify/import it or revert it—never blindly apply over an incident workaround.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

Terraform state/backendaws_* managed resourcesCI plan jobpolicy checks

Resource relationships

Terraform state maps resource addresses to real AWS objects. A manual console change alters AWS but not configuration/state intent; the next refresh/plan exposes drift and shows whether Terraform would revert, replace or require import/reconciliation.

Production pattern

Treat Git as desired-state authority. Restrict manual write access, run scheduled drift plans for critical stacks and reconcile deliberately rather than applying blindly over unknown production changes.

Representative Terraform

# CI drift job
terraform init -input=false
terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -out=tfplan
# exit 0 = no diff, 2 = changes/drift, 1 = error
# Gate apply until the drift is understood and reviewed.

Plan · rollout · verification

Compare Git commit, state and live AWS configuration. Identify who changed it through CloudTrail, decide whether code or AWS is correct, then update code/import/revert and require a clean reviewed plan before apply.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Run a read-only plan, inspect refresh differences and CloudTrail/Git history to identify who changed what. Reconcile explicitly and verify the resulting live behaviour.
Source / Provenance Motivity Labs

Q53L1CloudWatchEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

What are practical CloudWatch use cases?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 30–60 sec

I use CloudWatch for infrastructure metrics and alarms, centralized application/system logs, dashboards, log queries, custom metrics and event-driven operational actions. For EC2 specifically I combine native metrics with CloudWatch Agent for memory/disk/process telemetry. I alert on customer-impacting symptoms rather than every resource metric.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_cloudwatch_log_groupaws_cloudwatch_metric_alarmaws_iam_roleaws_iam_instance_profileaws_ssm_associationaws_sns_topic

Resource relationships

Native EC2 metrics provide CPU, network and status checks. The CloudWatch Agent on the instance publishes memory/disk and application logs. Alarms route actionable signals to the operations topic; SSM provides controlled host access and agent configuration without opening SSH.

Production pattern

Monitor user-visible availability and dependency health, not CPU alone. Standardize CloudWatch Agent configuration through SSM, define alarms as code and attach runbooks/dashboard links to alerts.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_cloudwatch_log_group" "app" {
  name              = "/platform/app"
  retention_in_days = 30
}
resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "cpu_high" {
  alarm_name          = "app-cpu-high"
  namespace           = "AWS/EC2"
  metric_name         = "CPUUtilization"
  statistic           = "Average"
  period              = 300
  evaluation_periods  = 3
  threshold           = 80
  comparison_operator = "GreaterThanThreshold"
  dimensions          = { AutoScalingGroupName = var.asg_name }
  alarm_actions       = [aws_sns_topic.ops.arn]
}
resource "aws_ssm_association" "cloudwatch_agent" {
  name = "AmazonCloudWatch-ManageAgent"
  targets { key = "tag:Role", values = ["app"] }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Validate metric dimensions and periods before apply. Generate a controlled test signal, confirm alarm state transition and notification delivery, verify memory/disk custom metrics and confirm SSM can reach the same hosts during an incident.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Inject a known failure/metric threshold, verify ingestion delay, dimensions, alarm transition, notification route and runbook. Check missing-data semantics and log retention.
Source / Provenance EPAM

Q56L2Cost optimisationDeloitteSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

How would you cut AWS infrastructure cost by 20%?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

To cut 20% I would first baseline spend by service/account/team and identify the largest controllable drivers. Then I right-size underutilized EC2/EBS, remove idle resources, apply Savings Plans/commitments to stable baseline, use Spot for tolerant burst, lifecycle storage and reduce avoidable data transfer/NAT paths. Every saving is measured against availability and performance so cost reduction does not become an outage.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_autoscaling_groupaws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configurationaws_budgets_budgetaws_cloudwatch_metric_alarmaws_scheduler_schedule

Resource relationships

Cost controls act on specific waste drivers: ASG/right-sizing controls compute quantity, schedules stop non-production idle capacity, lifecycle moves/expires cold S3 data and Budgets/alarms detect regressions. Commitment discounts are a purchasing decision layered on top of a stable baseline.

Production pattern

Start with measured usage and tagging, protect SLO-critical baseline, automate reversible savings first, then use Savings Plans/commitments for predictable residual load. Never reduce cost by removing HA blindly.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_budgets_budget" "monthly" {
  name         = "platform-monthly"
  budget_type  = "COST"
  limit_amount = var.monthly_budget
  limit_unit   = "USD"
  time_unit    = "MONTHLY"
}
resource "aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration" "logs" {
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.logs.id
  rule {
    id="tiering"; status="Enabled"
    transition { days=30, storage_class="STANDARD_IA" }
    transition { days=90, storage_class="GLACIER_IR" }
  }
}
# Non-prod start/stop schedules and ASG limits are environment-owned inputs.

Plan · rollout · verification

Baseline cost and SLO before change. Apply one saving class at a time, then verify instance utilization, latency/error rate, backup retention and monthly forecast. Roll back any saving that violates performance or recovery requirements.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Compare before/after normalized cost (per request/customer), utilisation, SLOs and forecast. Track realized—not theoretical—savings and rollback any change that breaches performance.
Source / Provenance Deloitte

Q58L2Terraform policyJPMorganChaseSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

How do you stop insecure Terraform changes reaching production?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

I prevent insecure Terraform reaching production by making production apply a controlled pipeline action. PRs run formatting, validation, security scanning, policy-as-code and a saved/reviewed plan; protected branches and required approvals gate merge; the pipeline assumes a short-lived least-privilege role. Direct console/manual applies are restricted and audited.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_iam_openid_connect_provideraws_iam_roleCI workflowpolicy-as-code checksTerraform plan artifact

Resource relationships

Developers change code through PRs. CI runs formatting, validation, security/policy checks and produces a saved plan. After approval, the runner federates through OIDC into a narrowly scoped apply role; no long-lived AWS keys are stored in CI.

Production pattern

Separate plan and apply permissions, require protected branches/reviews, pin tool/provider versions and make the reviewed plan the artifact that is applied. Use environment approvals for production.

Representative Terraform

data "aws_iam_policy_document" "ci_trust" {
  statement {
    actions = ["sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"]
    principals { type="Federated", identifiers=[var.github_oidc_provider_arn] }
    condition { test="StringLike", variable="token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub", values=["repo:org/repo:ref:refs/heads/main"] }
  }
}
resource "aws_iam_role" "terraform_apply" {
  name               = "terraform-prod-apply"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.ci_trust.json
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Open a test PR that violates policy and confirm it is blocked. For an approved PR, verify CloudTrail shows the federated CI role, the applied plan hash matches the reviewed artifact and no static access key is present.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Try a deliberately public SG/S3 policy or privileged IAM change and confirm the pipeline blocks it. Verify no long-lived cloud keys, production role trust conditions and CloudTrail attribution.
Source / Provenance JPMorganChase

Q59L2Terraform stateJPMorganChaseSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Secure team Terraform state, locking and tamper protection.

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

For team state I use a remote S3 backend with encryption, versioning, tightly scoped access and state locking so concurrent applies cannot corrupt coordination. Access is through short-lived CI/operator roles, not shared credentials. I protect the backend separately from workload stacks and test recovery from an earlier object version.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

S3 backendaws_s3_bucket_versioningaws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configurationaws_s3_bucket_policyaws_kms_key

Resource relationships

Terraform state is stored in an encrypted, versioned S3 backend. Native S3 lock files prevent concurrent writers. Bucket/IAM policy limits state access to the owning CI/team role; S3 version history is the recovery path for accidental deletion/corruption.

Production pattern

Use one tightly controlled backend per environment/ownership boundary. Enable versioning before production state exists, block public access, log/admin-protect the bucket and avoid manual state editing except controlled recovery.

Representative Terraform

terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket       = "company-prod-tfstate"
    key          = "compute/terraform.tfstate"
    region       = "eu-west-2"
    encrypt      = true
    use_lockfile = true
  }
}
# Provision the backend bucket separately with versioning, SSE-KMS,
# public-access block and least-privilege bucket policy.

Plan · rollout · verification

Test concurrent plan/apply locking in non-prod. Confirm state versions exist and only the CI/team role can read/write. For recovery restore the prior S3 object version, run terraform plan and reconcile to a no-surprise state before any apply.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Attempt concurrent plans/applies to confirm locking, inspect S3 versions, test restore in a sandbox, validate KMS/access denial and audit access through CloudTrail. Never manually edit state objects in normal operation.
Source / Provenance JPMorganChase

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

I bring a manual estate under Terraform incrementally. I inventory resources and dependencies, decide state boundaries/owners, write configuration that matches the live settings, then import resources and run plan until the diff is understood. I avoid importing everything into one state and avoid applying until Terraform would not accidentally replace production resources.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

import blocksmoved blocksaws_* resource definitionsremote backend

Resource relationships

Brownfield resources remain live while matching Terraform resource blocks are written. Import blocks map existing AWS IDs into specific resource addresses; a refresh/plan then reveals configuration gaps. Ownership is accepted only when the plan is non-destructive and reviewed.

Production pattern

Import by bounded stack/resource group, not the whole estate at once. Freeze or tightly control manual changes during adoption, preserve names/IDs, and use moved blocks for refactors after state is stable.

Representative Terraform

import {
  to = aws_instance.app
  id = var.existing_instance_id
}
resource "aws_instance" "app" {
  ami                    = var.ami_id
  instance_type          = var.instance_type
  subnet_id              = var.subnet_id
  vpc_security_group_ids = var.security_group_ids
  # Match live production attributes before first apply.
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Run refresh/plan immediately after import and require zero destructive changes. Compare critical attributes against AWS, document intentionally unmanaged fields and only then allow Terraform apply through the normal CI path.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
For each import verify ID/address, run plan, investigate every replacement/update, compare tags/policies/attachments and only apply after an expected near-zero or deliberate diff. Preserve rollback/state backups.

Q61L2IncidentsCMTSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Describe a production incident end to end.

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 2–4 min

I describe incidents in a consistent sequence: impact and scope, timeline/recent change, evidence, hypotheses, mitigation, root cause, permanent corrective action and prevention. I separate what I observed from what I assumed and quantify recovery where possible. The strongest example shows customer impact reduction and a systemic prevention, not just a command I ran.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_cloudwatch_log_groupaws_cloudwatch_metric_alarmaws_iam_roleaws_iam_instance_profileaws_ssm_associationaws_sns_topic

Resource relationships

Native EC2 metrics provide CPU, network and status checks. The CloudWatch Agent on the instance publishes memory/disk and application logs. Alarms route actionable signals to the operations topic; SSM provides controlled host access and agent configuration without opening SSH.

Production pattern

Monitor user-visible availability and dependency health, not CPU alone. Standardize CloudWatch Agent configuration through SSM, define alarms as code and attach runbooks/dashboard links to alerts.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_cloudwatch_log_group" "app" {
  name              = "/platform/app"
  retention_in_days = 30
}
resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "cpu_high" {
  alarm_name          = "app-cpu-high"
  namespace           = "AWS/EC2"
  metric_name         = "CPUUtilization"
  statistic           = "Average"
  period              = 300
  evaluation_periods  = 3
  threshold           = 80
  comparison_operator = "GreaterThanThreshold"
  dimensions          = { AutoScalingGroupName = var.asg_name }
  alarm_actions       = [aws_sns_topic.ops.arn]
}
resource "aws_ssm_association" "cloudwatch_agent" {
  name = "AmazonCloudWatch-ManageAgent"
  targets { key = "tag:Role", values = ["app"] }
}

Plan · rollout · verification

Validate metric dimensions and periods before apply. Generate a controlled test signal, confirm alarm state transition and notification delivery, verify memory/disk custom metrics and confirm SSM can reach the same hosts during an incident.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Use a timestamped timeline, before/after metrics, exact change commit/apply, validation of mitigation, and follow-up action owner. Confirm recurrence prevention with a test/game day.
Source / Provenance CMT

Q62L3Regional DRJPMorganChaseSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

If a whole Region fails, how do you avoid data loss?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

To avoid data loss in a regional failure I start with business RPO and design the data layer accordingly—cross-region replication for low RPO, plus independent backups for corruption/ransomware recovery. Compute and network capacity exist in the recovery region, and failover is tested. Zero data loss is not something I promise unless the chosen datastore and synchronous design actually support it.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_route53_health_checkaws_route53_recordaws_launch_templateaws_autoscaling_groupaws_backup_planaws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration

Resource relationships

Each failure domain has independent compute capacity and health signals. DNS/traffic routing shifts only to a stack that is actually healthy. Stateful data is replicated/backed up separately from EC2 so replacing compute does not lose business data.

Production pattern

Choose active-active when both sites can safely serve concurrent writes and the operational complexity is justified; active-passive is simpler but has failover/RTO trade-offs. Test failover, not just backup creation.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_route53_record" "app" {
  zone_id = var.zone_id
  name    = var.app_name
  type    = "A"
  set_identifier = "primary"
  failover_routing_policy { type = "PRIMARY" }
  alias {
    name                   = var.primary_alb_dns
    zone_id                = var.primary_alb_zone_id
    evaluate_target_health = true
  }
}
# A SECONDARY record points at the recovery stack.
# Backups/replication and AMI distribution are provisioned independently.

Plan · rollout · verification

Run a game-day: fail the primary health signal/stack, measure DNS/application failover, validate data currency and then fail back. Compare measured RTO/RPO to the business requirement and alarm on replication/backup lag.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Game-day regional failover: measure replication lag, achieved RPO/RTO, capacity, secrets/KMS/DNS dependencies and application consistency. Test failback as well as failover.

Q63L3ObservabilityJPMorganChaseSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

Design highly available logging across many services/regions.

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

I centralize logs into a dedicated security/observability account while keeping ingestion resilient to individual workload failure. Durable raw logs go to encrypted S3 with retention/replication as required; operational search can use CloudWatch Logs, OpenSearch or a SIEM. Producers have write-only delivery permissions and consumers have controlled read access.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

aws_cloudwatch_log_groupaws_cloudwatch_log_subscription_filteraws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_streamaws_s3_bucketaws_iam_role

Resource relationships

Application/account log groups feed cross-account subscriptions or Firehose into a central security/operations account. S3 provides durable retention, optional OpenSearch/SIEM serves interactive search and IAM/KMS policies separate producers from readers.

Production pattern

Centralize durable evidence while preserving account/region/source metadata. Use subscription destinations designed for scale, explicit retention, encryption and failure/dead-letter monitoring.

Representative Terraform

resource "aws_cloudwatch_log_subscription_filter" "central" {
  name            = "central"
  log_group_name  = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.app.name
  filter_pattern  = ""
  destination_arn = var.central_destination_arn
  role_arn        = aws_iam_role.logs_to_central.arn
}
# Central account provisions the destination/Firehose/S3 bucket and reader roles.

Plan · rollout · verification

Generate a known test event from two regions/accounts and confirm arrival with source metadata intact. Alarm on delivery errors/throttling, verify central readers cannot mutate source logs and test retention/replay procedures.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Kill an ingestion component/region where feasible and verify buffering/retry/no data loss, permissions, timestamps, duplicate handling, retention and query availability. Monitor ingestion lag and failed deliveries.

Q64L3Terraform at scaleEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

How do you isolate Terraform state across teams/environments?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

I isolate Terraform state by ownership and lifecycle boundary—typically account/environment/platform component—not by putting the whole company in one state. Each state has its own access policy and pipeline. Shared dependencies are consumed through explicit outputs, data sources or service contracts so teams do not gain write access to each other's state.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

terraform_remote_state / backendmodule.networkmodule.computemodule.storageaws_iam_role

Resource relationships

Reusable modules expose stable inputs/outputs; environment root modules instantiate them. Each environment/team owns a separate state boundary and CI role, preventing a compute change from locking or replacing unrelated network/application resources.

Production pattern

Separate state by lifecycle/ownership/blast radius, not by arbitrary file size. Keep providers/backends in root modules, pin module/provider versions and use distinct accounts/roles for environment isolation.

Representative Terraform

# environments/prod/main.tf
module "compute" {
  source = "../../modules/compute"
  vpc_id             = var.vpc_id
  private_subnet_ids = var.private_subnet_ids
  release_ami_id     = var.release_ami_id
}

# Backend configuration is supplied during init per environment, e.g.
# terraform init -backend-config=prod.s3.tfbackend
# Keep prod/dev state keys and IAM roles independent.

Plan · rollout · verification

Run init/validate/plan separately per environment. Verify a prod plan cannot read/write dev state and a module upgrade changes only intended resources. Test state locking and CI-role permission boundaries before team adoption.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Review blast radius of a plan, access matrix, lock independence and dependency cycles. Confirm team A cannot apply or read secrets from team B state unless explicitly required.
Source / Provenance EPAM

Q65L3State recoveryEPAMSOURCE-LINKED · CANDIDATE-REPORTED

How do you recover from deleted/corrupted remote Terraform state?

Source-linked candidate-reported question/paraphrase. Company badge reflects the cited report; architecture, answer, Terraform and validation below are our preparation layer.

Current / Check Architectureanimated check path · placement · failure boundary

Use this view to trace the current/check path first. For incident questions, the highlighted component is where evidence should be collected before changing configuration.

Corrected / Recommended Architectureanimated production target · HA/security/operations

Recommended target: explicit production ownership, private-by-default placement where applicable, observable health, controlled rollout and a defined recovery path.

Interview Answer 5–10 min

Recovery starts by stopping all applies. I determine whether the issue is state-object deletion/corruption or actual resource loss, then recover the last known-good remote state version or approved backup. I compare recovered state with live AWS using plan/refresh and reconcile carefully. Versioning and restricted backend access are the primary prevention controls.

Answer frame: requirement → architecture/path → evidence/operation → failure handling → trade-off.
Terraform Implementationproduction resources · relationships · HCL · controls

Production resources

S3 backendaws_s3_bucket_versioningaws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configurationaws_s3_bucket_policyaws_kms_key

Resource relationships

Terraform state is stored in an encrypted, versioned S3 backend. Native S3 lock files prevent concurrent writers. Bucket/IAM policy limits state access to the owning CI/team role; S3 version history is the recovery path for accidental deletion/corruption.

Production pattern

Use one tightly controlled backend per environment/ownership boundary. Enable versioning before production state exists, block public access, log/admin-protect the bucket and avoid manual state editing except controlled recovery.

Representative Terraform

terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket       = "company-prod-tfstate"
    key          = "compute/terraform.tfstate"
    region       = "eu-west-2"
    encrypt      = true
    use_lockfile = true
  }
}
# Provision the backend bucket separately with versioning, SSE-KMS,
# public-access block and least-privilege bucket policy.

Plan · rollout · verification

Test concurrent plan/apply locking in non-prod. Confirm state versions exist and only the CI/team role can read/write. For recovery restore the prior S3 object version, run terraform plan and reconcile to a no-surprise state before any apply.

Troubleshooting / Validation evidence first
Disable pipelines, identify last good state version and corresponding Git commit/apply, restore in a sandbox or controlled backend, run plan and inspect every proposed action. Resume applies only when state-to-reality mapping is trusted.
Source / Provenance EPAM
